name: Sort objects into categories
description: Student can sort a collection of objects into categories, which is the basis of categorical data.
exampleOfSuccess: The student sorts a mixed set of blocks into colours: red, blue and green piles.
commonError: Student sorts inconsistently, putting an object in the wrong group or making overlapping groups.
checkpointTask: Give the student a mixed collection. Ask them to sort it into clear groups and name each group.

name: Record data in a list
description: Student can record collected information as a simple list.
exampleOfSuccess: Asked about pets, the student writes a list: dog, cat, dog, fish, cat.
commonError: Student records only some responses, or writes counts before any data is collected.
checkpointTask: Ask the student a simple question of the class and have them record the answers as a list.

name: Record data with tally marks
description: Student can record data using tally marks while counting or observing.
exampleOfSuccess: Counting cars going past, the student makes a tally mark for each one and groups them in fives.
commonError: Student writes numerals instead of tallies, or forgets to mark the fifth tally across the group.
checkpointTask: Have the student tally a set of items or events as they occur. Check the tallies match the count.

name: Collect data to answer a question
description: Student can collect data to answer a simple question of interest.
exampleOfSuccess: To find the favourite fruit in the group, the student asks each person and records their answer.
commonError: Student collects data that does not match the question, or asks only some of the group.
checkpointTask: Pose a simple question (favourite colour, how we get to school). Ask the student to collect the data.

name: Choose a way to record data
description: Student can choose a sensible way to record data, such as a list, tally or symbols.
exampleOfSuccess: Asked to record how many of each pet, the student chooses a tally because it is quick while asking people.
commonError: Student picks a method that does not suit the data, or cannot say why they chose it.
checkpointTask: Pose a data-collection task. Ask the student how they would record it and why.

name: Record data with symbols or digital tools
description: Student can record categorical data using symbols or a simple digital tool.
exampleOfSuccess: The student records weather each day with sun, cloud and rain symbols, or enters tallies into a class app.
commonError: Student uses symbols that do not consistently stand for one thing each.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to record categorical data using a symbol key or a simple digital tool.

name: Make a one-to-one display with objects
description: Student can represent data with objects or drawings, using one object or drawing for each data value.
exampleOfSuccess: For pets in the class, the student places one block per child above the matching pet picture.
commonError: Student uses one object to stand for several values, breaking the one-to-one match.
checkpointTask: Give the student sorted data. Ask them to show it with one object per value above each category.

name: Create a pictograph
description: Student can create a pictograph where each picture stands for one item.
exampleOfSuccess: The student draws one apple per child who chose apple, in a row beside the fruit name.
commonError: Student draws pictures of different sizes or spacing so the rows cannot be fairly compared.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to turn sorted data into a pictograph with one picture per value.

name: Read a one-to-one display
description: Student can read a pictograph or one-to-one display and say how many are in each category.
exampleOfSuccess: Looking at a pictograph, the student says 5 children chose dogs and 3 chose cats.
commonError: Student miscounts the pictures, or reads the longest row as the category without counting.
checkpointTask: Show the student a pictograph. Ask how many are in each category.

name: Translate data between forms
description: Student can translate data from a list or display into a tally chart, or the reverse.
exampleOfSuccess: Given a list of votes, the student makes a matching tally chart with the right totals.
commonError: Student loses or double-counts values when moving between forms.
checkpointTask: Give the student data as a list. Ask them to make a matching tally chart.

name: Compare categories using frequencies
description: Student can compare categories by their counts, saying which has the most or least and how many more.
exampleOfSuccess: From a display, the student says dogs got the most, fish the least, and there were two more dogs than cats.
commonError: Student compares by row length by eye without counting, or cannot work out the difference between two counts.
checkpointTask: Show a display. Ask which category has most and least, and how many more one has than another.

name: Discuss what the data shows
description: Student can discuss the findings from a display, using it to answer the original question.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says the data shows most of the class walks to school, so walking is the most common way.
commonError: Student describes single counts without using them to answer the question that was asked.
checkpointTask: After the student makes a display, ask what it tells them about the original question.
